cases.why: INCIDENT 2026-07-29 (85 PDFs found, ZERO moved, reported 'Done — 2 step(s) completed') plus INCIDENT 2026-07-30 (the fix moved 85 including 8 out of a source repo, because the mutation guards still keyed on the singular tool name). Twelve top-level files exceed BATCH_EXPAND_MAX=8, so this exercises the move_files batch path — the shape rule 4 now tells the planner to draft — and the nested pair pins the top-level-only default.
cases.known_gap: FOUND BY THIS BENCH, 2026-08-03, and REPRODUCED 4/4 runs — not flaky. All 14 PDFs move, including the two inside downloads/project-src/assets. ROOT CAUSE, confirmed in code: the top-level-only partition lives in placeholder_resolver.partition_by_depth, which is reachable ONLY from resolve() — i.e. only when the drafted step still carries a 'PENDING:' placeholder. Here the revise/refine round writes the CONCRETE file list itself (logs show '_revise_node ... (refine)' and never 'Placeholder resolved in code'), so resolve() is never called and the partition, the truncated-source refusal AND the 'excluded N nested files' note are all bypassed. Same defect CLASS as 2026-07-30 (a guard keyed to one shape of the operation) and 2026-08-01 (_DIR_KEY covering reads but not writes) — third instance. The approval card does list all 14 paths, so the user CAN see them, but it carries no deferred-nested note and the documented default ('recursion is right for FINDING and wrong as a default for MUTATING') does not hold. NOT FIXED HERE: this round instruments and measures; changing the planner's bulk-mutation path needs its own falsification round.

cases.why: The pre-flight path guard: a WRITE/DESTRUCTIVE step whose target provably does not exist fails into the replan loop BEFORE the approval pause — the user is never asked to approve a guessed path. ⚠️ THIS CASE FIRST ASSERTED status_any=[failed, awaiting_choice] AND THAT EXPECTATION WAS WRONG: the plan legitimately ends COMPLETED with 'No matching files were found … nothing to do', which is placeholder_resolver's documented behaviour ('an outcome, not a failure'). Corrected to pin what actually matters — no delete tool ever ran, no approval was ever requested for a guessed path, and the user was told plainly that nothing was found. A test that asserts an incidental status instead of the guarantee is a test that reports a defect where there is none.
